params.body:
A settings page for readers, and annual plans that bill the way article 5 of the terms says.

## Settings, `/account/settings`

- **Profile:** name; address; password. A new address takes effect only from a link mailed to it (24 hours, used once). Signing in with Google, LinkedIn or Microsoft finds an account by its address, so an unproved address could hand an account someone else's sign-in. Changing the address or closing the account asks for the password when the account has one. A password change signs out every other browser. An account without a password gets a link to set one.
- **Plan and payments:** plan, next payment, the end of the annual term and the last day to cancel for it, Change plan and Cancel plan, billing details and payments (moved from `/account`).
- **Sign-in methods:** moved from `/account`. Linking and unlinking come back here.
- **Newsletter:** on and off. New subscriptions keep the double opt-in; an address confirmed before comes back at once.
- **Close your account** (`App\Accounts\Closing`):
  - On the free plan, at once.
  - On a paid plan, the plan is cancelled like any cancellation, and the account goes the night the plan ends (`accounts:close-due`, 01:15, after `billing:settle`). Until then "Keep my account" undoes both while the term's payments still run.
  - What goes: the account, sessions, keys, reads, and the newsletter address. What stays: the organisation's payments, kept for Trendwolves' accounts as the privacy notice says, and a row in `account_deletions`.
  - An account that can still be charged is never erased. The internal delete route uses the same code.
- `/account` keeps the plan, what it opens, AI tools and keys, and links to Settings. Team accounts see that their profile lives in the Observatory, and cannot close it here.

## Billing follows the terms

Article 5: every paid plan is annual, billed monthly, and "renews for successive twelve month terms unless cancelled at least thirty days before the renewal date". The code allowed a cancellation up to the last day and never renewed the term after year one. Now (`App\Billing\Subscriptions`):

- `cancelTakesEffect()`: cancelled at least `NOTICE_DAYS` (30) before the term ends, the plan ends with the term. Later, it has renewed and ends with the next term, and the cancel page says why.
- `renewTerms()` (in `settle`): a term that ran out without a cancellation renews for twelve months.
- A downgrade that takes effect at the end of a term starts a term of its own on the lower plan. Before, it dropped the term.
- `committed()` compared the term's end, which carries the time of day the plan was bought, with the next payment's midnight. A plan cancelled for the end of its year was charged a thirteenth time on the day it ended. It now asks whether the month a payment pays for ends inside the term (three days of slack for month lengths).

## Tests

- `AccountSettingsTest` (12) covers the page, the address link, the password, the newsletter, closing free and paid, keep, and erase refused while paying.
- `CancellationNoticeTest` (7) covers notice in time and late, renewal, the thirteenth payment, the last payment of a term, and a lower plan's own term.
- Existing tests now expect billing details, payments and sign-in methods on settings.
- Full suite 647/648. The one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which also fails on main in a worktree (`.git` is a file there). `pint --test` passes. Checked in a local site at desktop and phone width.

## Deploy

One migration (`users.closes_at`, `email_change_*`). The scheduler gains `accounts:close-due`.
params.title: Account settings, and annual plans billed as the terms say
